design_rationale:
WORKLOG / TEST DOSSIER - task 0 (factory_order_milestones_and_delays, env_0060 Ridgeline Window & Door)

[Step 0 draw] .venv/bin/python skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/draw_counts.py <diff> --tasks 2 printed: task 0 {"prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [6, 4, 4]}; task 1 {"prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [6, 4, 4, 6]}. Task 0 design: expedite fee 6 factors, hold-release requote 4, late-acknowledgment shift 4.

[Why this is a good test] The customer asks one plain thing - pay for a rush on her window order and hear the price. The scored number (fee_amount 941.40) cannot be read anywhere: the agent must (1) notice in the order record that the order is on hold, which the expedite rule refuses to price ("The expedite fee is not fixed until the order's status reads entered and, where the order was put on hold, a delay notice with cause customer hold records the ship date set when that hold was released."); (2) notice from the release rule that the requote waits on a late-acknowledgment notice ("The ship date set at a hold's release is worked out only after the order carries a delay notice with cause late acknowledgment whenever its acknowledgment was signed after the return window."), and that the acknowledgment signed 2026-07-22 came back after the window closed 2026-07-13 with no such notice on file; (3) compute three chained numbers in business days with U.S. federal holidays (Labor Day 2026-09-07 sits inside the expedite window), each with its own ladders read from the order ledger and from the window contract's change orders, measure visit and discount program. Difficulty comes from reading policy, reconciling records and calendar arithmetic; every tool is unambiguous by name.

[Scope snapshot] Occupied before this task: nothing (task 0). Claimed by task 0: order_ext_late_acknowledgment_shift (record_late_acknowledgment_notice_952cb75c, agent), order_ext_hold_release_requote (release_customer_hold_268345ec, agent), order_ext_expedite_fee (request_expedited_build_5d45bf5f, user). These are the only three computations the factory-order charter allows before production starts (late-acknowledgment shift, hold requote, expedite fee), so task 0 takes the whole pre-production space. Left for task 1 (draw: 3 prerequisite problems, factors [6,4,4,6]): the post-production space - remake delay notice (order_remakes, delay notice for a customer specification remake), customer remake charge (order_remakes charge), on-time guarantee credit (order_delays_and_guarantee) and branch storage fee (order_storage); four independent computations with their own tools, none overlapping task 0. Blueprint limits recorded for the difficulty: guarantee credit application is out of scope for any task because its event triggers a price credit in the window or door category (a write into another difficulty); charge waivers are full-amount by event definition and carry no factor; the only customer-owned acts in the charter are the acknowledgment signature, the hold request and the expedite request, of which only the expedite carries a number - so task 0 uses the expedite as its customer write and task 1 routes around the shortage (see task 1).

[Problem-tree card]
Root: order_ext_expedite_fee (fee_amount, target request_expedited_build_5d45bf5f, owner user, trigger on_request).
Edge 1: expedite_fee -> hold_release_requote. kind value_input, gate binding cur_t (current ship date read for the pull-in), form state. policy_source: "The expedite fee is not fixed until the order's status reads entered and, where the order was put on hold, a delay notice with cause customer hold records the ship date set when that hold was released." Four-point test: negated connective "not ... until"; waits on record-visible state (status entered + customer-hold notice); names no tool/id/code token; scope "where the order was put on hold" = exactly the edge condition. Exactly one write of this difficulty sets status entered and writes a customer-hold notice: the hold release (record_late_acknowledgment_notice writes a late_acknowledgment notice, request_expedited_build writes a charge). Opening falsity: initial_state.factory_orders.<fo>.status = on_hold; no customer_hold row in order_milestones. Resolved by release_customer_hold_268345ec (agent), at the customer's passive consent "so they can go ahead and take it off pause". Also flips the base gate order_expedite.expedite_before_production ("An expedite can be requested only while the order status is entered.").
Edge 2: hold_release_requote -> late_acknowledgment_shift. kind value_input, gate cur_t, form state. policy_source: "The ship date set at a hold's release is worked out only after the order carries a delay notice with cause late acknowledgment whenever its acknowledgment was signed after the return window." Affirmative "only after"; record-visible state (a late-acknowledgment delay notice); scope "whenever its acknowledgment was signed after the return window". Exactly one write records a late_acknowledgment cause: record_late_acknowledgment_notice_952cb75c. Opening falsity: acknowledgment_signed 2026-07-22 > window close 2026-07-13, order_milestones has no late_acknowledgment row, current_ship_date 2026-08-24.
Topological order: late-acknowledgment notice (step 7) -> hold release (step 9) -> expedite (step 11). Chain, no parallel edges. Deletion sensitivity (evalc skip runs): skip step 9 -> fee 644.40 instead of 941.40 and status stays on_hold; skip step 7 -> requote 46 (2026-09-25) instead of 59 (2026-10-08). Directions: one affirmative ("only after", the scheduling desk's wording for a date that is worked out) and one negated ("not fixed until", the billing desk's wording for a charge).
Customer write: the expedite request is the customer's own decision (blueprint: "asking for a hold or an expedite are the customer's own decisions that the agent hands over"), unlocked by the agent and run by her at the end of the order with the quoted fee. user_scenario names no prerequisite and no problem id; the pause and the late signature appear only in passive branches that fire after the agent raises them. The tools validate nothing (see prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block).

[Base-invariant card]
- Late-acknowledgment notice (subject order_delay_noticed): governing base policies order_acknowledgment_and_production, order_holds, order_delays_and_guarantee, order_remakes, order_expedite; none carries an eligibility gate on order_delay_noticed, so each is policy_scope. Inherited facts: the notice cause is late_acknowledgment; ack_on_time is a gate on the signature itself (order_milestone_logged) and its counting rule is reused verbatim ("Business days are counted starting the day after the order entry date, Monday through Friday excluding U.S. federal holidays, and a signature on the last day of the window is on time"): entry 2026-07-08, window 3 business days -> 2026-07-09, 07-10, 07-13; a signature on 2026-07-13 would be on time, 2026-07-14 is the first late day; the actual 2026-07-22 is late. Declared overwrite: the base sentence "When the acknowledgment is signed late, a delay notice with cause late_acknowledgment moves the current ship date later by the number of business days the signature came after the window." is replaced by the policy's shift sentence (lateness end date + paint-line, insert and cut-list days), which keeps the notice, its cause and the move of the current ship date.
- Hold release (subject order_hold_released): order_holds, gate hold_length (time). Anchor factory_orders.hold_start_date 2026-07-16, duration variants.hold_max_calendar_days = 60 for Custom Color Build, calendar days counted from the day after the hold start, relation not_after, inclusive: last permitted release 2026-09-14, first failing day 2026-09-15; release on 2026-08-10 = day 25, satisfied. Declared overwrite: "At release the current ship date is reset to the release date plus the class standard lead time in business days, and a delay notice with cause customer_hold records the new date." -> "At release the current ship date is reset to the requoted ship date worked out below, and a delay notice with cause customer hold records that new date." (the notice obligation is kept). Other order_holds sentences (no hold after production start, no guarantee credit for holds, no storage on a held order) stay in force and are untouched.
- Expedite fee (subject order_charge_assessed): order_agg_customer_orders (no gate on charges -> policy_scope; the fee stays on its own order), order_expedite gate expedite_before_production ("An expedite can be requested only while the order status is entered.") - false at the opening (on_hold), true after step 9 (prior_step:9 evidence); class Custom Color Build has expedite_available true. order_remakes gate customer_charge_basis and order_storage gate after_free_period apply literally to every order_charge_assessed row; the expedite policy declares two scoped overwrites stating that each condition governs its own charge kind alone, naming both the expedite fee (this policy) and the sibling charge kind (storage fee / remake charge) as outside it, and that every remake charge / storage fee stays under it. Formula overwrite: "The expedite fee is the class fee per unit times the units on the order, never less than the class minimum fee, booked on the request date." -> the per-unit charge plus add-ons sentence, which keeps "never less than the class minimum expedite fee" and "booked on the request date".

[Business-object card] One customer (Dolores Hartwell), one window contract RW-26-204718 (Ridgeline 2200 Series Vinyl, showroom sale, senior program, status ordered, released 2026-07-06), one factory order FO-2026-21437 (Custom Color Build, 12 units). Every order-side aggregate is scoped to this order's milestone rows (3 seeded: capacity notice 2026-07-14, acknowledgment 2026-07-22, glass received 2026-08-04). Window-side evidence is filtered to window_contract_id of the order: change orders 2026-06-30 (exterior_color 7 openings, grilles_between_glass 4 openings - one change order, the first, so no change-order fee), the oversize_surcharge line of the final measure (2 openings, 192.00, a company line that does not count as a change order) and the completed final measure 2026-05-01 (12 openings, 2 oversize). Excluded: the booking deposit row (2558.16 = 30 percent of 8527.20) feeds no factor. Nothing has been waived, credited or reversed on the order. The tools write onto factory_order_id, the narrowest key.

[Factor card - late-acknowledgment shift (4 factors, result 25 = 2026-09-04)]
1 signature_count_endpoint (parameter - it chooses only which date ends the count): tiers signed-during-hold -> count to hold start / factory notice after window -> count to notice date / otherwise -> count to signature. Evidence: hold_start_date 2026-07-16, acknowledgment 2026-07-22, no customer_hold notice. Tier taken: during hold, 3 business days. Baseline (count to signature, 7 days) -> 32. Near-miss: the factory-capacity notice of 2026-07-14 lies after the window and before the signature; a reader who misses the hold tier counts to it (1 day).
2 paint_line_rebooking (parameter, cross-difficulty window): 7 colored openings vs 12 units -> at least half -> +2. Baseline 0 -> 23.
3 insert_hardware_reorder (parameter, cross-difficulty window): grilles change order -> +2. Baseline 0 -> 23.
4 cut_list_regeneration (method - the long-lateness tier computes a count from the plant's weekly Friday cut-list run instead of adding a constant): raw signature lateness 7 business days (> 5) -> business days after Wednesday 2026-07-22 through Friday 2026-07-24 = 2. Baseline 0 -> 23.
Whole baseline (lateness to signature 7, no extras) -> 23 (2026-09-02). The cut-list tier reads the raw signature lateness, a record quantity, never the endpoint factor's output.

[Factor card - hold-release requote (4 factors, result 59 = 2026-10-08)]
1 requote_basis (method, multi-source: hold length AND acknowledgment signed on every non-fall-through tier): hold 25 days, signed -> slot kept: current ship date 2026-09-04 + 17 business days of hold = 2026-09-30. Baseline (release + 30 business days = 2026-09-22) -> 51.
2 seasonal_reload (parameter): August release -> +3. Baseline -> 56.
3 capacity_resequencing (parameter): one factory_capacity notice dated less than three whole calendar months before the release -> +2. Baseline -> 57.
4 glass_rereservation (parameter): no glass-supplier notice, glass received 2026-08-04 -> +1. Baseline -> 58.
Whole baseline -> 43 (2026-09-22). Trap: requoting from the committed date 2026-08-19 or from the stale 2026-08-24 instead of the date after the late-acknowledgment notice.

[Factor card - expedite fee (6 factors, result 941.40)]
1 pull_in_rate (parameter): target 2026-09-08, current ship 2026-10-08, 22 business days pulled in -> 70/unit. Baseline 55 -> 792.90. Trap: using the committed date gives 0 days -> 40/unit.
2 volume_structure (method): 12 units on the acknowledgment covering the most units > 10 -> 10 x 70 + 2 x 35 = 770. Baseline 12 x 70 -> 1004.40.
3 paint_line_priority (parameter, cross-difficulty window): 7 colored >= 6 -> 7 x 20 = 140. Baseline -> 815.40.
4 oversize_handling (parameter, cross-difficulty window): 2 oversize -> 2 x 20 = 40. Baseline -> 905.40.
5 holiday_overtime (parameter): Labor Day inside (2026-08-10, 2026-09-08] -> 12 x 8 = 96. Baseline -> 855.00.
6 program_discount (parameter, cross-difficulty window): senior -> 10 percent. Baseline -> 1046.00.
Whole baseline: max(225, 12 x 55) = 660.00. Multi-source factor of the task: requote_basis. Cross-difficulty factors of the task: paint_line_rebooking, insert_hardware_reorder, paint_line_priority, oversize_handling, program_discount (window rows seeded for this customer).

[Seed rows and why each exists] customers (identity: phone 6145550127, ZIP 43205, DOB 1958-09-03 - aged 67 at signing, consistent with the senior program's minimum age 65). window_contracts RW-26-204718 (discount program, the contract the order builds; status ordered because released). window_transactions: booking deposit 2026-04-20 (release needs the full deposit), completed final measure 2026-05-01 with 2 oversize openings (oversize factor), oversize surcharge line 2026-05-01 (2 x 96.00, required by the window charter for oversize openings), exterior color 7 x 118.00 = 826.00 and grilles 4 x 52.00 = 208.00 on 2026-06-30 while the contract was measured (paint and insert factors). factory_orders: the held order (removing it removes the task). order_milestones: capacity notice (capacity factor and the endpoint near-miss; without it the capacity days drop out of the requote, 57 instead of 59), acknowledgment 2026-07-22 (late signature; deleting it removes the late-acknowledgment obligation, the slot-kept tier and the volume units), glass received 2026-08-04 (glass factor; deleting it gives 58). Automatic clauses checked: no hold auto-release is due (day 25 of 60); no storage, guarantee or remake obligation exists before production; the capacity notice is 1 of the escalation count 3; production has not started because the order is held, so no system transition is owed.

[Persona] Dolores Hartwell, a retired librarian, warm and a little formal. She volunteers only the goal (pay for a rush on her window order and hear the price) and the natural situation (family moving in this fall). Identity on request: name, phone 6145550127, then ZIP 43205 or DOB September 3, 1958; contract RW-26-204718 and FO-2026-21437 only if asked. Passive branches: if the agent mentions the hold, she confirms she asked for the July pause during the kitchen remodel and says to take it off pause; if the agent says a notice or a new ship date must go on the order because her acknowledgment came back late, she agrees; asked about the signing date she gives only "a Wednesday toward the end of July" and defers to the records. She runs the expedite request herself with the quoted fee and ends the call when the fee shows as booked. She never names the release or the notice, never states a date or amount gold uses, and never corrects the agent.

[Standard solution] find_customers(phone) -> verify(phone + ZIP) -> find_factory_orders -> find_order_milestones -> find_window_contracts -> find_window_transactions; record the late-acknowledgment notice with 25 (2026-09-04); release the hold with 59 (2026-10-08); unlock and hand over the expedite request; the customer submits 941.40.

[Verification run] Authoring evaluator (scratch evalc.py, replaying gold writes with the real tools before each step and evaluating each policy compute; deleted at the end) printed:
order_ext_late_acknowledgment_shift step 7 => 25 | baseline 23; signature_count_endpoint 32, paint_line_rebooking 23, insert_hardware_reorder 23, cut_list_regeneration 23.
order_ext_hold_release_requote step 9 => 59 | baseline 43; requote_basis 51, seasonal_reload 56, capacity_resequencing 57, glass_rereservation 58.
order_ext_expedite_fee step 11 => 941.4 | baseline 660.0; pull_in_rate 792.9, volume_structure 1004.4, paint_line_priority 815.4, oversize_handling 905.4, holiday_overtime 855.0, program_discount 1046.0.
skip L for H: 46; skip H for E: 644.4.
Gates for task 0 (repo root, --task 0): check_extended EXTENDED OK; check_task_tools TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK; replay_tasks REPLAY OK; check_solvability SOLVABILITY OK; check_compute COMPUTE OK; check_grounding GROUNDING OK; check_cross_fire SCOPE OK.

[Rule <-> compute sweep] Late-acknowledgment shift: ent_t/win_t <- "The return window closes ..."; sig_date/ack_n/sig_t <- "The late-acknowledgment shift is the business days of signature lateness ..."; hold_t, rel_last, held_at_sig, fac_last, fac_t, end_t, lat_n <- the end-date sentence (both endpoints inclusive, counting from the day after the window closes); colored/paint_days, grilles/hardware/insert_days, raw_n/cut_days <- their tier sentences; shift <- "...all added as whole business days before the revised ship date is counted"; rev_t <- "counted in business days starting the day after the current ship date"; result <- "written as the number of calendar days from the handling date". Reverse: every sentence of the rule is claimed (the replaced_by sentence states the notice effect the tool performs). Requote: slot/remaining/standard paths, hold length in calendar days from the hold start to the release date, the 30-day threshold and the class maximum, month tiers, three-month capacity window, glass tiers, extras counted after the date first set. Expedite: target date, pull-in endpoints (day after target through current ship date, inclusive), unit structure, the three add-ons, minimum applied to the sum, discount after the minimum, single rounding at the end (RND(..., 2) on the final binding only).

[Places most easily got wrong] counting lateness to the signature instead of the hold start; counting the capacity notice; skipping the late-acknowledgment notice and requoting from 2026-08-24; requoting from the release date (standard lead) despite a short hold with a signed acknowledgment; forgetting Labor Day in the target date or the holiday add-on; using the committed date for the pull-in; applying the discount before the minimum or rounding intermediate amounts; booking the fee while the order is still on hold.

[Solvability vs GT] Step 7 policy_scope evidence on the five governing policies (no gate on delay notices). Step 9 hold_length bound to factory_orders.<fo>.factory_order_id, frozen_time and hold_start_date, temporal boundary 2026-09-14 / 2026-09-15. Step 11 expedite_before_production bound to prior_step:9's factory_orders delta (status entered); customer_charge_basis and after_free_period retired by the declared overwrites (policy_scope entries). Required inputs (phone, ZIP or DOB, consent to release, consent to the notice, the fee acceptance) all cite verbatim persona text.

[Draft recomputation from visible context] Masking compute and gold: from the published rule text, the order record (on_hold, entered 2026-07-08, current 2026-08-24, hold 2026-07-16), the milestones (capacity 2026-07-14, signature 2026-07-22, glass 2026-08-04) and the window rows, a reader concludes the expedite cannot be priced on a held order, the release cannot be requoted before the late-acknowledgment notice, and computes 3+2+2+2 = 9 business days -> 2026-09-04 (25), 17+6 business days -> 2026-10-08 (59), and 770+140+40+96 = 1046 -> 941.40 - identical to gold. No second reading found: every tier condition is disjoint as stated and each date endpoint is stated inclusive.

[Revision log] (1) Symptom: replay flagged 12 dangling foreign keys. Cause: empty reference fields seeded as "" are read as references. Change: empty reference ids seeded and written as null (seed rows and the three tools). Re-run: REPLAY OK. (2) Symptom: check_compute "history NOT load-bearing" for the late-acknowledgment shift and the expedite fee. Cause: both read the acknowledgment only through LATEST, which the history-zeroing test leaves untouched. Change: both now count the acknowledgment checkpoints first ("signature lateness" and "units on the signed order acknowledgment" are defined only when a signed acknowledgment is on record; without one the lateness is nil and no unit is acknowledged). Re-run: COMPUTE OK, scored values unchanged (25 / 59 / 941.40). (3) The earlier plan's credit-application root was dropped: the credit-application event triggers a price credit in the window or door category, which a tool of this difficulty may not cause.


[Rework round 2 - item closure for task 0] (F-G12 / T0-O1) signature_count_endpoint chooses only the end date of the lateness count and is relabelled parameter; cut_list_regeneration becomes the policy's method factor - beyond 5 business days late the order waits for the plant's weekly Friday cut-list run, so the added days are counted from the day after the signature through the first Friday after it (a computed count instead of a constant); 3-5 days late adds a fixed 1, fewer adds nothing. On this world the run is Friday 2026-07-24, 2 days, so every task-0 figure is unchanged (25 / 59 / 941.40; signature_count_endpoint 32, cut_list_regeneration 23). requote_basis and volume_structure were already shape-changing methods. (F-G15 / F-G5) The expedite volume structure reads the acknowledgment covering the most units (MAX, so a later partial re-acknowledgment cannot shrink it) and its fall-through prices every unit on the order, matching the baseline. (F-G6) The capacity window is worded as the computation counts it: notices dated less than three whole calendar months before the release. (F-G8 / T0-O3) The late-acknowledgment and hold rules now say the class enumerations (business_days_late, release_date_plus_standard_lead) describe only the standard method and the rule's own requote governs. (F-G2) No task-0 ladder collapses in another build class (pull-in 70 / 40 / class 45 or 55; day adders are absolute). T1-O1 tool change also applies here: the late-acknowledgment notice tool keeps the later of the revised date and the standing projection; on this world 2026-09-04 is later than 2026-08-24, so the terminal state is unchanged. Gates re-run after the change: EXTENDED OK, TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK, REPLAY OK, SOLVABILITY OK, COMPUTE OK, GROUNDING OK, SCOPE OK.
user_scenario:
You are Dolores Hartwell, a 67-year-old retired school librarian in Columbus, Ohio. You speak warmly and a little formally, you like to have things explained once, plainly, and you keep a folder with every Ridgeline paper on the kitchen table while you talk. In April you bought twelve Ridgeline 2200 Series Vinyl windows at the showroom, with a dark exterior color on some of them and grilles between the glass on a few; that window order is now with the factory. Your daughter's family is moving in with you in the fall and you would like the new windows in sooner, so you are calling to pay for a rush on the factory build of your window order. That is the whole reason for the call: you want the rush put in, and you want to know what it costs before you agree to it.

You open by saying you would like to pay to have your window order rushed at the factory and asking what that would cost. You do not offer anything else up front. When the agent asks who you are, you give your name, Dolores Hartwell, and the phone number on your account, 6145550127. If the agent asks for another detail to confirm it is you, you give your ZIP code, 43205; if they ask for your date of birth instead, it is September 3, 1958. If they ask for your window contract number you read it off your copy: RW-26-204718; the factory order number on the acknowledgment paper is FO-2026-21437, which you read out only if asked for it.

You let the agent look things up and do whatever office work is needed on the order to get the rush going; you are happy for them to handle that for you. If the agent mentions that your order is on hold or paused, you confirm that you asked for the pause in July while your kitchen was being redone, and that the kitchen is finished, so they can go ahead and take it off pause. If the agent tells you a notice or a new projected ship date has to be put on the order because your signed acknowledgment came back late, you say you did sit on that paper for a while and that is fair, go ahead. If the agent asks when you signed the acknowledgment, you say it was a Wednesday toward the end of July and that their records will have the exact date. You do not remember any of the ship dates you were told and say so if asked.

The rush itself you want to agree to yourself. When the agent tells you the rush fee, you accept it, and when they hand you the expedite request to submit, you submit it on your factory order with exactly the fee amount the agent gave you. Once you see that the rush fee has been booked, you thank the agent for the help and say goodbye.

Cut-list regeneration (method): the signature came 7 business days after the window (more than 5), so the order waits for the next weekly Friday cut-list run, adding the business days after Wednesday 2026-07-22 through Friday 2026-07-24 = 2. Shift 3+2+2+2 = 9 business days from the current ship date 2026-08-24 gives 2026-09-04 (2026-08-25 through 2026-09-04, no holiday inside); 2026-09-04 is 25 calendar days after the handling date 2026-08-10.

edges.condition: factory_orders.status is entered and, for an order that was put on hold, order_milestones carries the order_delay_noticed row with delay_cause customer_hold written at that hold's release, its revised_ship_date equal to factory_orders.current_ship_date.
edges.policy_source: The expedite fee is not fixed until the order's status reads entered and, where the order was put on hold, a delay notice with cause customer hold records the ship date set when that hold was released.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: At 2026-08-10 the order is still on hold (status on_hold since 2026-07-16) and no customer-hold delay notice has been written, so the order's status does not read entered and no notice records a ship date set at a release.
evidence: initial_state.order_milestones.f8d1c845-2b7a-4eec-a250-440770641c33.delay_cause = factory_capacity (the only delay notice; no customer_hold notice exists)
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The release write sets factory_orders.status to entered and current_ship_date to 2026-10-08 and adds an order_delay_noticed row with delay_cause customer_hold and revised_ship_date 2026-10-08; the expedite fee's pull-in then counts 22 business days (rate 70) instead of 0 (rate 40).

edges.condition: Whenever the order's acknowledgment_signed checkpoint is dated after the return window, order_milestones carries an order_delay_noticed row with delay_cause late_acknowledgment for the order, and factory_orders.current_ship_date already reflects that notice's revised_ship_date.
edges.policy_source: The ship date set at a hold's release is worked out only after the order carries a delay notice with cause late acknowledgment whenever its acknowledgment was signed after the return window.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The acknowledgment_signed checkpoint is dated 2026-07-22, after the return window closed on 2026-07-13, yet the order carries no delay notice with cause late_acknowledgment and its current ship date still reads the capacity date 2026-08-24.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The late-acknowledgment write adds an order_delay_noticed row with delay_cause late_acknowledgment and revised_ship_date 2026-09-04 and moves current_ship_date to 2026-09-04, the date the slot-keeping requote starts from.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a chain, late acknowledgment -> hold release -> expedite fee, with no parallel prerequisites. Each order is pinned by a prerequisite sentence: the hold release rule says the ship date set at release is worked out only after the late-acknowledgment notice is on the order, and the expedite rule says the fee is not fixed until the order reads entered with the hold notice recorded. Running the release first would requote from 2026-08-24 (46 days, 2026-09-25) and leave the late-acknowledgment notice to move the released date afterwards, which gives a different terminal state, so the stated order is the only correct one.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the release (step 9) and replaying the rest: the order stays on_hold with current ship date 2026-09-04, the pull-in counts 0 business days, the rate falls to 40 and fee_amount becomes 644.40 instead of 941.40; factory_orders.status stays on_hold instead of entered and no customer_hold notice is written.

Skipping the late-acknowledgment notice (step 7): the requote starts from 2026-08-24, so days_to_new_ship_date becomes 46 (2026-09-25) instead of 59 (2026-10-08); the terminal order also lacks the late_acknowledgment notice row.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario raises only the rush (expedite) and its cost. It never mentions a hold release, a late-acknowledgment notice or a ship date being reset; the pause and the late signature appear only in passive branches that fire after the agent itself brings them up ('If the agent mentions that your order is on hold or paused ...', 'If the agent tells you a notice or a new projected ship date has to be put on the order ...'). No problem id appears in it.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: record_late_acknowledgment_notice_952cb75c, release_customer_hold_268345ec and request_expedited_build_5d45bf5f each look up the order only to copy its customer reference, unit count and standing ship date, then write unconditionally: none reads the order status, the acknowledgment, the hold or any other delay notice, none returns an error or a hint. The notice tool keeps the later of the revised date and the standing projection because a delay notice only moves the projection later (the event's own meaning), which is not a check. An expedite requested while the order is still on hold is booked exactly as given, and the missing release shows only in the terminal records.
